narrative.overview: SERENDIPIA is an observatory of chance, not a chord website. The fretboard is a sky chart, each chord is a star, the progression is a constellation the player traces, and suggestions are "hallazgos". One system lives in two themes: night (near-black violet, print grain, lilac ink) and day (silver-grey, near-black ink, vivid turquoise fills, deep-turquoise strokes). Color is information and ornament never sits on data.
keyCharacteristics: Two themes, one meaning for function colors and note roles
Sections and controls must read as such: framed, raised, visible pressed state
Flat tonal layering with hairline frames and small structural shadows
Engraved serif display, distressed at night and clean by day
Desk shell with no page scroll at 1024x640 and up

rules.name: The Color-Is-Information Rule
rules.body: Hue is reserved for harmonic function and note role; never decorative, never different between themes.

rules.name: The Print-Grain Rule
rules.body: A fixed noise overlay is texture only and never carries meaning.

rules.name: The Numeral Rule
rules.body: Readouts use tabular numerals; chord names use lining numerals; no oldstyle numerals are set in the build.

rules.name: The Serif-For-Names Rule
rules.body: Engraved serif is for chord names and glosses only; anything you click is Jost.

rules.name: The Desk-Fits Rule
rules.body: On the desk nothing may push the page into scroll; new content fits a row budget or lives in a popover.

rules.name: The Ornament-Never-On-Data Rule
rules.body: Ornament sits behind or beside content, with no pointer events, and never overlaps data.

rules.name: The Sections-And-Buttons-Must-Read Rule
rules.body: Every section has a visible header and framed edge; every control is a filled or framed shape with a visible pressed state.

rules.name: The Day/Night Eclipse Rule
rules.body: Themes differ in ground, ink, accent and grain, never in meaning; switching goes through setTheme with the circle origin at the toggle.

dos: Do express harmonic function with the four function hues and note roles with their shapes; keep both identical in meaning across themes.
Do frame every section as a module with a header, and give every control a raised or filled shape with a visible pressed state.
Do use tabular numerals for readouts and lining numerals for chord names.
Do keep meaningful text at 11px or larger, controls at 28px or larger on the desk and 44px on touch, and visible 2px focus outlines.
Do respect reduced motion: twinkle, ripples and the eclipse become static or instant.
Do add tokens as --cc-* pairs for both themes at once.
donts: Don't put ornament (mesh, ripples, hatch, orbit, barcode) over data or give it pointer events.
Don't use a function hue decoratively, or encode a note role by color alone.
Don't use turquoise as text on the day ground; use the deep turquoise.
Don't add page scroll to the desk shell, or wrap the top bar.
Don't reintroduce the legacy Riso paper, blue, orange and yellow tokens that remain in tailwind.css; they are leftovers.
Don't build white-card diagram grids or generic dark neon DAW chrome.
